Many thanks for your help) will share more feedback if anything.

Congratulations! We’re freeing you from the daunting prospect of watching Trump’s biggest speech of the year alone in your apartment. Entertainment is something we believe is compatible with, if not essential to, political engagement. 

With that in mind, we wanted to bring a carefully selected group of people together to sync, think, and drink about the state of our union. Here’s what the night has in store: 

:cocktail::pizza: — We’ll start with food and drinks to take the edge off in getting to know new people

Grace Weinstein is a Recount OG who recently launched “Who Broke It” on Substack, covering the emerging in-crowds and imminent crash outs in political content creation.  

AlexxMedia hosts the brand new YouTube call-in show “AM Mornings” — you can also see him co-hosting “Flagrant” and running a budding podcast studio empire. 

The Bench gives all of us — from the politically curious to the all-out addicted — a place to meet, programming to watch, and the space to create the future of media and politics.

messages.text: Hi there - Pumped to be on board here. I've spent the last few days getting set up and navigating the content upload options. A ramble on my proposed strategy here as it relates to my existing content, which is primarily news articles living on websites that I've written for a couple dozen publications. I think they could all translate to a SaySo carousel format (multiple media slides), but it appears I'd need to come up with or leverage some sort of template for the visuals. I'm thinking 3-4 slides total per SaySo post encompassing a mix of 1) the article headline, 2) a pull quote, 3) a visual and 4) a colorful portion of the article that allures folks to read more. This approach aligns with my general vibe. These visuals would be accompanied by the post copy (I'd need to draft) and the article link (source). Perhaps opposed to other folks that have existing videos/content at this phase to simply transfer over here, I would need to create these slides/graphics and copy from scratch-ish which will be a heavier initial lift than anticipated. Surely, once my templates and process irons out here, it will be seamless. Thoughts on this approach and/or any tools I may be able to leverage from here? Once I hear back, I'll roll on a first carousel, likely using some of my newer pieces, e.g. <https://www.travelandleisure.com/gayle-king-celeb-check-in-11908163> or <https://www.lonelyplanet.com/articles/best-time-to-visit-las-vegas>. Thank you!

Leaving my feedback a little early this week, had a few issues this week with the new version:

-Got an email saying one of my episodes was struck for sexually explicit content, and I don't know how. Think it was miscategorized. However, it used the Description instead of the Title to tell me this, so it took me a while to figure it out. Also, it says "Under content moderation" still even though I got the email that it was banned.

-In general, having only the description and not the Title shown when you click on a post feels off. If there's a title AND a description, I think we should be able to see both. Right now, the Title only appears in the Digest.

-I have about 4 posts that have grey thumbnails on my profile page. Videos still work, but not the thumbnails.

-A few times I tried uploading this week, first day or so on the new version, and they didn't go up. I should have 110 but have 108 posts, not sure what happened there.

-Took me a minute to figure out where to create a post. Upper left-hand corner wasn't intuitive at first, but that may just be getting used to a new interface, not an actual design issue.

-Would be nice in the future to know the exact dimensions of a Daily Digest vs. Explore preview. Since the Explore doesn't list titles or descriptions, it's hard to know what each video is about without watching it. It's just a talking head and rarely is there on-screen text to explain the concept or topic, which would draw folks in. Feels like the Explore Page should also have a Title for each preview of a video.
